newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA BANCOREX HAS NEW CHIEF, POLICE HEAR EX-BOSS.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA BANCOREX HAS NEW CHIEF, POLICE HEAR EX-BOSS.

text.p: Florin Ionescu was named on Friday as chairman of the leading state-run Bancorex SA commercial bank to replace Razvan Temesan, reportedly in police custody, a central bank official said on Friday.
National Bank spokesman Adrian Vasilescu told Reuters Ionescu was appointed after a Bancorex shareholder's meeting decided to sack Temesan and his deputy Alexandru Ghiba.
Late on Friday, the state television said Temesan had been taken in police custody for 24 hours after a five-hour meeting with police officers "who asked him to show some documents."

"Razvan Temesan has been invited and heard at the Penal investigations department. A committee was created to investigate claims related to Razvan Temesan," an Interior Ministry statement said without elaborating.
The General Prosecutor's office issued an order forbidding Temesan to leave Bucharest for the next 30 days pending investigations.
The state television also showed Temesan being taken under guard to the Bucharest's police penal investigation department.
It was not immediately clear whether there were any charges brought against Temesan as neither police officials nor prosecutors were available for comment.
Vasilescu said he was not aware of the police action.
Under the law prosecutors have to decide within 24 hours whether to issue an arrest warrant against Temesan or free him.
Bancorex would not be affected by the management shake-up, Vasilescu said, adding that Ghiba had been replaced by Maria Constantinescu.
"Ionescu and Constantinescu are good professionals. The bank is solid and on the right track," Vasilescu said, adding that he ruled out any "possible run on the bank."
He declined to comment on Temesan's removal, saying it was "an internal affair" of Bancorex's shareholders.
Temesan was appointed Bancorex chairman in 1994.
Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA, specialised in foreign trade financing, handles the bulk of foreign exchange trading on the local market.

The latest data show the bank has share capital of 93.2 billion lei, with the State Ownership Fund holding 63 percent and private ownership funds some 27 percent. The rest goes to corporations and individuals.
Last year, Banking rating service Thomson BankWatch awarded Bancorex a LC-1 short-term local currency debt rating, implying a very high likelihood of interest and principle for the bank.
This month, Moody's Investors Service assigned Bancorex's long-term deposits a B1 rating and a not-prime for the short-term ones.
